entries.clue: Investigates frontless dresses (5)

indicatorNotes.frontless: without its front: the first letter goes

blocks.note: PROBES = investigates, minus its first letter P

annotation.surface: Someone is looking into dresses that have no front panel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dresses' reads as a verb beside 'investigates', but it is the plural noun, garments like robes.
annotation.definitionFit: Robes are long loose garments, a kind of dress.

entries.clue: Item of fruit came up hard? One gets soft (7)

indicatorNotes.gets: the one takes the soft letter after it

blocks.note: rose = came up, as the sun does

annotation.surface: A piece of fruit turned out hard, and then one goes soft.
annotation.walkthrough: The hard/soft contrast looks like a comment on ripeness, but both words are single-letter abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: The red seed pod a rose leaves after flowering is eaten or made into syrup, so botanically it counts as a fruit.

entries.clue: Defender holding line in NZ colours? (5)

indicatorNotes.holding: BACK holds the L inside it

blocks.note: a back is a defender in football or rugby

annotation.surface: A rugby defender wears the New Zealand kit and holds the line.
annotation.walkthrough: New Zealand's rugby team, the All Blacks, plays in black, hence the question mark on a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Black is the colour New Zealand's national sides wear.

entries.clue: Unusual prison pictures revealing elevated characters (14)

indicatorNotes.Unusual: the letters are put in an unusual order

annotation.surface: Odd photographs from a jail show some high-ranking people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Elevated characters' suggests important people, but the characters are letters written above the line.
annotation.definitionFit: Superscription is writing placed above, and superscript characters sit raised above the line.

entries.clue: Quiet introduction of scale of temperature (4)

indicatorNotes.introduction of: the introduction of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A gentle start to a temperature scale.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'of' in the middle does double duty: it belongs to the indicator phrase and also appears in the answer as itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Soft and quiet both describe a low sound.

entries.clue: Science, kind curtailed aboard ship (cutter) (8)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: its tail, the last letter, is cut off
indicatorNotes.aboard: on board the ship, so inside SS

blocks.note: SORT = kind, minus its last letter T

annotation.surface: A science and a sort of vessel are named, with a cutter, itself a type of boat, in brackets.
annotation.walkthrough: A cutter is also a small sailing ship, which the bracketed word leans on, but here it means something that cuts.
annotation.definitionFit: The bracketed word, which sounds like a boat, defines scissors by their only job: cutting.

entries.clue: Closed down in the past, beset by US lawman (6)

indicatorNotes.beset by: surrounded by the letters of FED

blocks.note: a fed is an FBI agent

annotation.surface: A business shut down long ago while hounded by an American federal agent.
annotation.walkthrough: Fed is American slang for a federal agent, usually of the FBI, which is what makes him a US lawman.
annotation.definitionFit: Fold is the standard verb for a business going under, and folded matches closed down in tense.

entries.clue: Mapmakers interrupted by recall of finished work (4)

indicatorNotes.interrupted by: to be interrupted is to have something break into the middle, so the turned UP splits OS
indicatorNotes.recall of: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: OS = Ordnance Survey, the UK's national mapping agency

annotation.surface: Cartographers are distracted by a completed piece being recalled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finished work' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'finished' is wordplay and 'work' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for work and names a single composition or book, often numbered in a catalogue.

entries.clue: Composer favouring including acceptable arrangement for five (9)

indicatorNotes.including: to include is to hold within, so PRO holds OK inside it
indicatorNotes.arrangement for: an arrangement puts the letters of five into a new order

annotation.surface: A composer likes including a suitable arrangement for a quintet.
annotation.walkthrough: An 'arrangement for five' sounds like music scored for five players, which suits a composer, but it is an anagram of the word five.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sergei Prokofiev, the Russian who wrote Peter and the Wolf, is one composer.

entries.clue: Flickering screen with unknown landscape (7)

indicatorNotes.Flickering: the letters flicker into a new order

blocks.note: y is an unknown in algebra

annotation.surface: A flickering screen shows a view of the countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: Letters like x, y and z stand for unknowns in algebra, which is how 'unknown' gives a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: scenery and landscape both mean the view of natural surroundings.

entries.clue: Lined beach and pier up? Impossible to work out (14)

indicatorNotes.up: the letters are torn up and remade

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters; 'and' just joins the parts

annotation.surface: A seafront lined with a beach and a pier is thrown into confusion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks as if it belongs with 'pier', but it is the anagram indicator, in the sense of things being all broken up.
annotation.definitionFit: Something indecipherable cannot be worked out or read.

entries.clue: Quantity of current beginning to matter in motionless crushing machine (5,4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of matter is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: AMP and M go inside STILL

blocks.note: an amp is a unit of electric current

annotation.surface: A measurement of electricity flows into a machine that has stopped.
annotation.walkthrough: An ampere, the amp for short, is the unit of electric current, so a quantity of current is measured in them.
annotation.definitionFit: A stamp mill crushes ore with heavy pounding stamps.

entries.clue: Executioner’s tool? Never sit to have head cut off! (5)

blocks.clueFragment: sit to have head cut off
blocks.note: POSE = sit (for a portrait), minus its first letter P

annotation.surface: A plea never to sit for the executioner, because heads get cut off.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures beheading, the wrong method of execution for a noose; the question mark flags the grim joke.
annotation.definitionFit: The hangman's noose is the tool of an execution by hanging.

entries.clue: One putting up alfresco holidaymaker? (5)

blocks.note: one who hikes prices, putting them up
someone walking in the open air on holiday

annotation.surface: Someone pitching a tent on an outdoor holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' suggests a tent, but it means raising, as in a price hike.
annotation.definitionFit: A hiker walks outdoors for pleasure, and one who hikes raises something.

entries.clue: Dock worker to deserve being at sea? (9)

indicatorNotes.being at sea: confused, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Does a man who works the docks earn a place at sea?
annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits a dock worker's world, which hides its use as the anagram indicator meaning bewildered.
annotation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at a dock.

entries.clue: Conveyor of brief message after vehicle died (8)

blocks.note: d = died, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A short note arrives after a car death.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' reads as the order of events, but here it is the prefix POST.
annotation.definitionFit: A postcard carries a short message through the mail.

entries.clue: Excellent and wise person producing big American event (5,4)

blocks.note: an owl is a byword for wisdom

annotation.surface: A brilliant, wise figure puts on a big show in America.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay breaks one letter later than the enumeration, so the solver must ignore the space in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the NFL's championship game, a huge American event.

entries.clue: Criticise volume one? Biography cut short before end of story (6)

indicatorNotes.cut short: the last letter is cut off
indicatorNotes.end of: the last letter of the word

blocks.note: LIFE = biography, minus its last letter E

annotation.surface: A reviewer pans the first volume of a biography that stops short of the story's end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Volume one' reads as the first book of a set, but it splits into V and I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to vilify is to speak ill of someone, the harshest end of criticising.

entries.clue: American begged to follow vehicle on rails, getting run down (8)

indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come after, so PLED is placed after TRAM

blocks.note: pled is the American past tense of plead

annotation.surface: An American pleaded while chasing a tram, only to be knocked down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' marks the US spelling: pled where British English says pleaded.
annotation.definitionFit: Run down, as by a vehicle or a stampede, means knocked over and crushed underfoot.

entries.clue: Short time out to get family item for table (6)

blocks.note: a nap is a short rest

annotation.surface: A brief break lets the family fetch something for the dinner table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short time out' reads like a sports break, but it is a brief sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: Table linen is where the napkin belongs, so the clue defines it by where it lives.

entries.clue: A lot of birds felt sun shimmering (7)

indicatorNotes.shimmering: the letters waver into a new order

annotation.surface: A flock of birds feel the sun's shimmering heat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A lot of birds' sounds like a big flock, but a nestful is only as many as one nest holds.
annotation.definitionFit: A nestful is the brood of birds a nest holds.

entries.clue: One runs from greatest opponent on record (8)

indicatorNotes.runs from: one R, run, runs away from the word

blocks.note: an arch-rival is your greatest opponent
one R (r = runs in cricket) leaves ARCHRIVAL

annotation.surface: An athlete runs away from their fiercest competitor, a record-holder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On record' reads like a sporting record, but it is the definition: kept in the archives.
annotation.definitionFit: Archival means kept on record in archives.

entries.clue: Send up a lot of tough seafood (7)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of the word, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: to lob is to send a ball high up
STERN = tough, minus its last letter N

annotation.surface: Someone complains that a lot of the seafood is tough.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Send up' suggests mockery, but it means a lob, a high throw.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lobster is one of the shellfish sold and eaten as seafood.

entries.clue: Urge competition - something seen with soldiers? (6)

blocks.note: a cup is a competition, like the FA Cup

annotation.surface: A contest is urged on, with something alongside the troops.
annotation.walkthrough: Soldiers are strips of toast in British homes, dipped into a boiled egg standing in its eggcup; the question mark marks the pun on army soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: An eggcup holds the boiled egg that toast soldiers are dipped into.

entries.clue: Plan - an excellent idea? - to get behind beds (9)

indicatorNotes.to get behind: to get behind something is to go after it, so GEM follows STRATA

blocks.note: strata are layers or beds of rock
a gem of an idea is an excellent one

annotation.surface: A scheme: a clever notion about getting behind the beds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beds' suggests furniture, but these are geological beds, layers of rock.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stratagem is a cunning plan, originally a military one.

entries.clue: What going into pub set back? (5)

annotation.definition: What going into pub set back?

indicatorNotes.going into: going into something means entering it, so EH is placed inside
indicatorNotes.set back: to be set back is to be put backwards, so BAR reads RAB

annotation.surface: A question: what happens when drinking in pubs causes a setback?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rehab is what someone whose drinking has set them back goes into.
annotation.definitionFit: Rehab treats people whose lives have been set back by drink.

entries.clue: Spirit? Try a touch of tequila (5)

indicatorNotes.a touch of: just a little of the word: its first letter

blocks.note: a judge hears or tries a case

annotation.surface: Want a spirit? Try some tequila.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'tequila' paint a bar, but spirit means courage.
annotation.definitionFit: Spirit in the sense of courage: to take heart or lose heart is to gain or lose spirit.

entries.clue: Ring-bearer? Father the same, bearing ring (5)

indicatorNotes.bearing: to bear is to carry, so FR and DO carry the O between them

annotation.surface: A man at a wedding carries the ring, as his father did.
annotation.walkthrough: Frodo Baggins carries the One Ring in The Lord of the Rings; the surface suggests a wedding page.
annotation.definitionFit: Frodo is the hobbit who bears the Ring in Tolkien's story.

entries.clue: Serviceperson’s angry speech with VIP (9)

blocks.note: a rant is an angry speech

annotation.surface: A soldier's furious tirade in front of a dignitary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Serviceperson' suggests the armed forces; here the service is a church service, and the 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A celebrant is the person who leads a religious service.

entries.clue: Flower idly avoiding a zone (4)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: the word does without these letters

blocks.note: A plus Z for zone, both removed from LAZILY

annotation.surface: A flower sits idly, keeping out of a particular area.
annotation.walkthrough: Removing A and Z from LAZILY leaves L-ILY.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the lily is one flower among many, and the plain 'Flower' covers it.

entries.clue: Wanting content soup used veg (4)

indicatorNotes.Wanting content: without their contents, so only the outer letters stay

annotation.surface: Someone unhappy with their soup had vegetables put in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting content' sounds like a dissatisfied diner; it means lacking contents, the inner letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Spud is informal for potato, a vegetable.

entries.clue: Go into American heartland, heading away (5)

indicatorNotes.heading away: the heading of a word is its first letter, and it goes away

blocks.note: CENTER, the American spelling of centre, minus its first letter C

annotation.surface: Someone travels into the middle of the United States, then leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American' flags the US spelling CENTER, which loses its C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to enter a room is to go into it.
